gospel_1925.csv.note: Paul Robeson recorded Steal Away on July 27, 1925 in Camden, with Lawrence Brown at the piano. Victor 19742 was issued in 1925. The label reads Steal Away. The spiritual is also known as Steal Away to Jesus.

gospel_1928.csv.note: Blind Willie Johnson recorded both sides in Dallas on December 3, 1927, singing alone. Jesus Make Up My Dying Bed was issued on Columbia 14276-D on January 20, 1928. If I Had My Way I'd Tear the Building Down was issued on Columbia 14343-D on August 30, 1928. Willie B. Harris sings on his 1930 records, not these. The order follows the issue dates.

gospel_1930.csv.note: Can't Nobody Hide from God is Blind Willie Johnson with Willie B. Harris, recorded in Atlanta on April 20, 1930 and issued on Columbia 14556-D. It is not a Willie Mae Williams record.

gospel_1937.csv.note: Thomas A. Dorsey wrote Precious Lord, Take My Hand in August 1932, after his wife and infant son died. He published it in 1938. The first record is the Heavenly Gospel Singers, Bluebird B-6846, released on March 10, 1937.

gospel_1939.csv.note: Sister Rosetta Tharpe recorded This Train in New York on January 10, 1939. Decca 2558 was issued that year, with her on vocal and electric guitar.

gospel_1947.csv.note: Mahalia Jackson recorded Move On Up a Little Higher for Apollo on September 12, 1947. It was the first gospel record to sell a million copies.

gospel_1951.csv.note: The Soul Stirrers recorded Jesus Gave Me Water on March 1, 1951, with Sam Cooke on lead. Specialty 802 was issued in May 1951, backed with Peace in the Valley. Lucie Campbell wrote it.
